_meta.indication: AEMCOLO is indicated for the treatment of travelers' diarrhea (TD) caused by non-invasive strains of Escherichia coli in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled superiority trial; subjects randomized 3:1 to rifamycin 400 mg BID orally or placebo for 3 days.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult travelers (≥18 years) with travelers' diarrhea, conducted at sites in Guatemala and Mexico.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to last unformed stool (TLUS) in the intent to treat (ITT) population.
pivotal_trials.result: Median TLUS significantly shorter with rifamycin (46.0 hours) vs placebo (68.0 hours), p < 0.0008; clinical cure 81.4% rifamycin vs 56.9% placebo, p < 0.0001.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, multicenter non-inferiority trial comparing rifamycin (200 mg po BID for 3 days) versus ciprofloxacin (500 mg po BID for 3 days), 1:1 randomization.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with travelers' diarrhea; conducted at 17 sites in India and 1 site each in Ecuador and Guatemala.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: TLUS in the full analysis set (FAS) population.
pivotal_trials.result: Median TLUS 44.3 hours rifamycin vs 40.3 hours ciprofloxacin.

nct_ctgov.title: Rifamycin SV-MMX® Tablets Versus Ciprofloxacin Capsules in Acute Traveller's Diarrhoea

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >2%) are headache and constipation. In the active-comparator trial, headache occurred in 3.3% of AEMCOLO patients vs 1.9% ciprofloxacin. Discontinuation due to adverse reactions occurred in 1% of patients (abdominal pain 0.5%, pyrexia 0.3%).
target_moa: An ansamycin antibacterial that inhibits bacterial DNA-dependent RNA synthesis by binding DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, blocking RNA chain initiation.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to / discussed at an FDA advisory committee, as there were no issues that would benefit from an advisory committee discussion.

basis.text: The NDA was reviewed under Priority review.

summary.text: AEMCOLO was submitted as a priority review 505(b)(2) NDA for the treatment of travelers' diarrhea caused by non-invasive E. coli in adults, and was approved November 16, 2018 based on a placebo-controlled superiority trial (C2009-0201) with supportive evidence from active-comparator trial RIT-1/AID. It was not an accelerated approval and was not referred to an advisory committee.

Rifamycin demonstrated superiority to placebo for the treatment of travelers' diarrhea due to non-invasive E. coli in a randomized, double-blind multi-center, placebo-controlled trial in adult travelers (Study C2009-0201). A second active-controlled trial comparing rifamycin to ciprofloxacin provided supportive evidence of efficacy (Study RIT-1/AID).
Your application for AEMCOLO was not referred to an FDA advisory committee as there were no issues that would benefit from an advisory committee discussion.
